technical_and_design_decisions: U1: Implement tenant-based ZK namespace as a configurable sub-path prefix (e.g., /<tenant-name>/<path>) injected via a TenantContext bean; existing ZK paths migrated only for metadata isolation, not for stored business data.

U2: Use Spring Security with an in-memory/DB-backed UserDetailsService and a simple login form/session for the Admin server; remove the file-based credential store and ensure no password is ever logged.
U3: Create the maintenance branch directly from the current master HEAD as 'maintenance/<minor-version>' (e.g., maintenance/1.0.2) and update CI/release scripts to publish MINOR artifacts from it.

U4: Treat deprecated public APIs and the legacy module-definition download mechanism as deletion candidates after grep-based call-site analysis; Shell and Admin-UI modules are audited to remove now-unused commands/buttons.
U5: Take the direct ZK connection approach for xd-shell (no LB) and add a shell command to discover the Admin server's random port via the ZK ensemble, so the shell can target it directly.
U6: Migrate to the Kafka 0.9+ new consumer (kafka.clients.consumer.KafkaConsumer) API, replacing the high-level consumer; rerun the previously failing integration tests against the new client.
U7: Deliver only the research spike and a design specification for Motion-JPEG-based ingest (decoder library candidates, container support); full implementation is out of scope for this increment.
U8: Add a boolean property 'cluster.view.showMessageRates' to servers.yml bound to a @ConfigurationProperties POJO; UI table/column for message rates is rendered conditionally based on this flag.
All activities are performed by a single developer on a pre-existing Spring XD codebase with established build, test, and CI infrastructure.
assumptions: A standard workday of 8 hours is used for all effort estimates.
The target system is Spring XD (Spring eXtreme Data); the generic Spring Framework description in the spec is context, not a development target.
Development environment, source repository, build tooling, and CI pipeline already exist and are functional.
Existing automated test harness is reused; no new test framework is introduced.
U3 is a Git/CI configuration task, not a code-development task.
U7 is treated as a research spike and design deliverable; no production-grade streaming pipeline is built.
No major architectural refactoring is required beyond what is explicitly stated in the user stories.
All code changes follow existing project conventions; no new style guides or governance are introduced.
Cross-cutting overhead (design, integration test, documentation, code review) is sized for a single developer.

activities.activity_description: Review the 8 user stories, clarify acceptance criteria, produce a short technical design note covering affected modules (ZK layer, Admin server, xd-shell, Kafka module, servers config), and identify cross-cutting impacts.

activities.activity_name: U1 - Implement tenant-based ZK namespace isolation
activities.activity_description: Add tenant-namespace configuration, modify ZK path construction to prefix the tenant identifier, and update related unit/integration tests to verify isolation between tenant profiles.

activities.activity_name: U2 - Username/password authentication for Admin server
activities.activity_description: Replace file-based credentials with a username/password login flow: configure Spring Security, add a login page/API, secure admin endpoints, ensure passwords are never written to logs, and add tests for auth and access control.

activities.activity_name: U3 - Set up MINOR release maintenance branch
activities.activity_description: Create the maintenance branch from master, update CI/release configuration so MINOR releases (e.g., 1.0.2) are built and published from this branch, and document the branching policy.

activities.activity_name: U4 - Clean up deprecated functions and Shell/Admin-UI modules
activities.activity_description: Identify deprecated APIs (including module-definition download) and all call sites, remove them, prune obsolete Shell commands and Admin-UI components, and update tests to reflect the cleaned-up surface.

activities.activity_name: U5 - xd-shell access to Admin server's random port
activities.activity_description: Spike: research direct ZK connection vs LB for xd-shell/admin interaction; design a solution that lets the shell discover the Admin server's random port via ZK; implement and test the shell-side command/pointer.

activities.activity_name: U6 - Upgrade Kafka bus to new consumer and rerun tests
activities.activity_description: Update the Kafka message bus module to the 0.9+ consumer rewrite API, adapt surrounding code, and rerun the previously failing tests until they pass on the new client.

activities.activity_name: U7 - Motion-JPEG research spike and design spec
activities.activity_description: Research feasibility of Motion-JPEG-based audio/video ingest for predictive analytics (including opencv platform constraints), and produce a design spec covering format handling, decoder choices, and integration points.

activities.activity_name: U8 - servers.yml flag to enable/disable message rates in cluster view
activities.activity_description: Add the new configuration property to servers.yml and the bound configuration bean, implement conditional rendering of message-rate information in the cluster view, and add tests for both enabled and disabled states.

Run the full integration test suite (or representative subset) covering all changed modules together, fix regressions introduced by the U1, U2, U4, U5, U6, and U8 changes, and verify end-to-end behavior.

Update user/admin/developer documentation: tenant configuration, admin authentication, branching policy, removed deprecated APIs, shell port discovery command, Kafka upgrade notes, and the new servers.yml flag.

activities.activity_name: Code review, quality assurance, and release preparation
activities.activity_description: Self-review of all changes, static analysis/checkstyle cleanups, final QA pass, and preparation of release notes summarizing the 8 delivered items.
